**Table A-6 CPU interface responses**

| Response                             | ID  | Parameters in the<br>first 16-bit<br>transfer | Data in<br>subsequent<br>transfers | Description                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------------------------|-----|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Clear Acknowledge                    | 0x4 | Bit [4]: V                                    | -                                  | Acknowledges that the CPU interface received a Clear<br>command for a specified interrupt.                                        |
| Downstream<br>Control<br>Acknowledge | 0xB | -                                             | -                                  | Acknowledges that the CPU interface received a<br>Downstream Control command from the Redistributor.                              |
| Quiesce<br>Acknowledge               | 0x9 | -                                             | -                                  | Acknowledges a Quiesce command, and confirms that<br>the Redistributor to CPU interface is in the quiescent<br>state.             |
| Release                              | 0x3 | Bits[7:6] ID length<br>Bit[4]: V              | INTID                              | Releases control of an interrupt when the CPU interface<br>cannot handle the interrupt, and provides a reason for<br>the release. |

All other command and response IDs are reserved. If the CPU interface receives a reserved ID, this constitutes a protocol error, see *[Software generation of protocol errors and packet errors on page](#page-888-0) A-889*.

A command packet has an equivalent handshake response packet that acknowledges the command. There are two exceptions to this rule:

- The [Clear](#page-897-0) and [VClear](#page-909-2) commands are both acknowledged by a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) response with a bit field in the header that indicates which command is acknowledged.
- The [Set](#page-905-0) and [VSet](#page-909-1) command packets are acknowledged by a [Release](#page-904-1) response or an [Activate](#page-895-0) command. This means that the [Activate](#page-895-0) command also has the semantics of a response with respect to the [Set](#page-905-0) and [VSet](#page-909-1) commands. When an [Activate](#page-895-0) command is used, the Redistributor acknowledges that command with an [Activate Acknowledge](#page-895-1) response. [Release,](#page-904-1) [Activate](#page-895-0), and [Activate Acknowledge](#page-895-1) packets all have a bit field in the header that indicates whether the response is to a [Set](#page-905-0) or [VSet](#page-909-1) command.

Responses to a [Set](#page-905-0) or [VSet](#page-909-1) command are dependent on system contexts and events on the CPU interface. A [Release](#page-904-1) response occurs when a pending interrupt that has been forwarded to the CPU interface cannot be maintained as pending or activated by the CPU interface. This can occur, for example, when:

- The interrupt group of the INTID is disabled.
- The highest pending physical interrupt is updated by a [Set](#page-905-0) command before it is activated.
- The highest pending virtual interrupt is updated by a [VSet](#page-909-1) command before it is activated.

#### <span id="page-891-1"></span>**A.3.1 Rules associated with the downstream Redistributor commands**

The following rules affect the generation of Redistributor commands:

- When [GICR\\_WAKER.](#page-727-0)ProcessorSleep == 0, the first packet that is issued to the CPU interface must be a [Downstream Control](#page-900-0) packet. This packet communicates the number of supported Security states, together with the physical and virtual INTID lengths that the GIC Stream Protocol interface supports.
- There can never be more than one outstanding [Downstream Control](#page-900-0) command, and a Redistributor must only generate response packets until the [Downstream Control](#page-900-0) command is acknowledged.
- On receipt of a [Set](#page-905-0) command, a CPU interface is required to release the previous pending physical interrupt back to the Redistributor.
- Unless restricted by another rule in this section, two [Set](#page-905-0) commands can be generated and outstanding at the same time, and the Redistributor must be able to accept an [Activate](#page-895-0) command for a physical interrupt when a [Set](#page-905-0) command is transferred.

- On receipt of a [VSet](#page-909-1) command, a CPU interface is required to release the previous pending virtual interrupt back to the Redistributor.
- A [VSet](#page-909-1) command must only be generated when the Redistributor is able to accept an [Activate](#page-895-0) command for a virtual interrupt while the [VSet](#page-909-1) command is being transferred.
- The Redistributor can only issue a single Clear to the CPU interface and must wait for a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) (with V == 0) before another can be issued. While a Clear is outstanding, no further "Physical Interrupt" packets except acknowledgments can be issued to the CPU interface.
- The Redistributor can only issue a single [VClear](#page-909-2) to the CPU interface and must wait for a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) (with V == 1) before another may be issued. While a [VClear](#page-909-2) is outstanding, no further "Virtual Interrupt" packets can be issued to the CPU interface.
- There can never be more than one outstanding [Quiesce](#page-903-1) command, and a Redistributor must only generate response packets until the [Quiesce](#page-903-1) command is acknowledged with a [Quiesce Acknowledge.](#page-904-2)
- A Redistributor must not send a [VSet](#page-909-1) or [VClear](#page-909-2) command to a CPU interface that does not support GICv4. The mechanism for determining whether GICv4 is supported is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED.
- A [VSet](#page-909-1) and [VClear](#page-909-2) command can specify an INTID:
  - For GICv4.0, in the LPI range.
  - For GICv4.1, in the LPI or SGI range.

A CPU interface does not send a [Deactivate](#page-898-1) in response to the deactivation of vSGI received in response to a [VSet](#page-909-1).

#### **A.3.2 Rules associated with the upstream CPU interface commands**

The following rules affect the generation of CPU interface commands:

- There can never be more than one outstanding [Upstream Control](#page-906-0) command, and a CPU interface must wait for an [Upstream Control Acknowledge](#page-908-0) before issuing another [Upstream Control](#page-906-0) command.
- There can never be more than one outstanding [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command. This means that a CPU interface must wait for a [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command to be acknowledged before issuing another [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command. The CPU interface can continue to send other commands before receiving the [Deactivate Acknowledge](#page-900-1) response.
- There can never be more than one outstanding [Generate SGI](#page-902-1) command. This means that a CPU interface must wait for a [Generate SGI](#page-902-1) command to be acknowledged before issuing another [Generate SGI](#page-902-1) command. The CPU interface can continue to send other commands before receiving the [Generate SGI Acknowledge](#page-903-2) response.
- Before issuing a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) response with the V bit set to 0, the CPU interface must issue any [Release](#page-904-1) commands that are required to move the physical interrupt specified in the [Clear](#page-897-0) command to the inactive state on the CPU interface.
- Before issuing a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) response with the V bit set to 1, the CPU interface must issue any [Release](#page-904-1) commands that are required to move the virtual interrupt specified in the [VClear](#page-909-2) command to the inactive state on the CPU interface.
- Before issuing a [Quiesce Acknowledge](#page-904-2) response, all other outstanding commands from the Redistributor must be acknowledged, and a [Release](#page-904-1) command must remove any pending interrupts on the CPU interface.
- A CPU interface always responds to Set commands in the order SETs are received.
- A CPU interface always responds to Virtual Set [\(VSet](#page-909-1)) commands in the order [VSet](#page-909-1) commands are received.
- A [Release](#page-904-1) command with V==1 can specify an INTID:
  - For GICv4.0 in the LPI range.
  - For GICv4.1 in the LPI or SGI range.

- For a [Clear,](#page-897-0) or [VClear,](#page-909-2) with INTID=1023, the CPU interface responds with an acknowledge, but otherwise ignores the command.
- If the GIC Stream connection is quiescent, on receiving a [Downstream Control](#page-900-0) packet the first packet that is issued by the CPU interface to the Redistributor is a [Downstream Control Acknowledge](#page-901-0) packet.

#### <span id="page-893-0"></span>**Priority-based routing**

When [ICC\\_CTLR\\_EL3](#page-237-0).PMHE == 0, or [ICC\\_CTLR\\_EL1.](#page-232-0)PMHE == 0:

• The CPU interface must not issue a [Release](#page-904-1) command for a pending SPI because the priority of the SPI is equal to or less than that indicated by [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1](#page-266-0).

**Note**

The CPU interface might still issue a [Release](#page-904-1) command for a pending SPI for other reasons, such as the SPI belonging to a group that is disabled in the CPU interface, or in response to receipt of a [Clear](#page-897-0) command from the IRI.

When [ICC\\_CTLR\\_EL3](#page-237-0).PMHE == 1 or [ICC\\_CTLR\\_EL1](#page-232-0).PMHE == 1:

- The CPU interface must issue an [Upstream Control](#page-906-0) command, with the identifier 0x02, when the PE successfully writes to [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1](#page-266-0):
  - If multiple writes to [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1](#page-266-0) occur before the CPU interface issues the [Upstream Control](#page-906-0) command, the GIC can combine these writes into a single command.
- The CPU interface can issue a [Release](#page-904-1) command for a pending SPI with a priority that is equal to or less than the value in [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1,](#page-266-0) if the [Set](#page-905-0) command was received between the architectural execution of the instruction that updated [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1](#page-266-0) and the receipt of the [Upstream Control Acknowledge](#page-908-0) command that indicates that the new [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1](#page-266-0) value has been observed. Whether a [Release](#page-904-1) is generated in this situation is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED.
- The CPU interface must not issue a Release command for a pending SPI with a priority that is greater than the value in [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1](#page-266-0) if the Set command was not received between the architectural execution of the instruction that updated [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1](#page-266-0) and the receipt of the [Upstream Control Acknowledge](#page-908-0) that indicates that the new [ICC\\_PMR\\_EL1](#page-266-0) value has been observed.

| Note |  |
|------|--|
|------|--|

The CPU interface might still issue a Release command for a pending SPI for other reasons, such as the SPI belonging to a group that is disabled in the CPU interface or in response to receipt of a [Clear](#page-897-0) command from the IRI.

#### <span id="page-894-1"></span><span id="page-894-0"></span>**A.4 Alphabetic list of command and response packet formats**

This subsection lists all the command and response packet formats in alphabetical order. The heading for each command or response subsection includes a label, ICC or IRI, that indicates the agent that generated the packet.

#### <span id="page-895-0"></span>**A.4.1 Activate (ICC)**

The CPU interface sends an Activate command when acknowledging an interrupt. When the Redistributor receives the Activate command, it sets the interrupt to the active state. The CPU interface must send an Activate command only when Redistributor action is required, as follows:

- For SPIs, SGIs, and PPIs, where the Redistributor must clear the pending bit for edge-triggered interrupts, and set the active bit.
- For LPIs where the Redistributor must clear the pending bit.

The [Activate](#page-895-0) command generated by the CPU interface, unlike other commands, also acts as a response to a [Set](#page-905-0) or [VSet](#page-909-1) command:

• A [Set](#page-905-0) or [VSet](#page-909-1) command results in a [Release](#page-904-1) response or Activate command. An Activate command acknowledges the original [Set](#page-905-0) command. The Activate command is itself acknowledged using an [Activate](#page-895-1)  [Acknowledge](#page-895-1) response from the Redistributor.

[Figure](#page-895-2) A-2 shows the Activate command format.

![](_page_895_Figure_8.jpeg)

a. If the command includes this field, bits[31:24] are 0.

**Figure A-2 Activate**

#### <span id="page-895-2"></span>In [Figure](#page-895-2) A-2:

- ID length indicates the number of INTID bits the Activate command includes. See *[Supported INTID sizes on](#page-888-1)  page [A-889](#page-888-1)* for more information.
- V indicates the original command to which the Activate command corresponds:
  - **0** The Activate corresponds to a [Set](#page-905-0) command.
  - **1** The Activate corresponds to a [VSet](#page-909-1) command.
- INTID is the value that the CPU interface returns after a valid read of [ICC\\_IAR0\\_EL1,](#page-252-0) [ICC\\_IAR1\\_EL1](#page-254-0), or [GICC\\_IAR.](#page-756-1)

![](_page_895_Figure_17.jpeg)

During legacy operation, the INTID that is returned for SGIs includes the source PE in the [GICC\\_IAR.](#page-756-1)Source\_CPU\_ID field.

#### <span id="page-895-3"></span><span id="page-895-1"></span>**A.4.2 Activate Acknowledge (IRI)**

The Redistributor sends an Activate Acknowledge response to confirm receipt of an [Activate](#page-895-0) command, and confirms that the effects of the activate operation are visible to the Redistributor and other PEs. [Figure](#page-895-3) A-3 shows the Activate Acknowledge response format.

![](_page_895_Figure_21.jpeg)

**Figure A-3 Activate Acknowledge**

|      | In Figure A-3 on page A-896, V indicates the original command to which the Activate Acknowledge corresponds:                                      |  |  |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--|--|
| 0b0  | The Activate Acknowledge corresponds to a Set command.                                                                                            |  |  |
| 0b1  | The Activate Acknowledge corresponds to a VSet command.                                                                                           |  |  |
| Note |                                                                                                                                                   |  |  |
|      | There is no requirement for Activate Acknowledge commands to be issued in the same order as the Activate<br>command to which they are responding. |  |  |

#### <span id="page-897-0"></span>**A.4.3 Clear (IRI)**

The Clear command clears the specified pending interrupt. [Figure](#page-897-2) A-4 shows the Clear command format.

![](_page_897_Figure_3.jpeg)

a. If the command includes this field, bits[31:24] are 0.

**Figure A-4 Clear**

#### <span id="page-897-2"></span>In [Figure](#page-897-2) A-4:

- ID length indicates the number of INTID bits that the Clear command includes. See *[Supported INTID sizes](#page-888-1) [on page](#page-888-1) A-889* for more information.
- INTID identifies the interrupt to be cleared.

The CPU interface must always respond to a Clear command with a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) response where V == 0.

If the interrupt is pending in the CPU interface, the CPU interface must issue a [Release](#page-904-1) response, or an [Activate](#page-895-0) response that remains outstanding for the interrupt before it issues a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) command.

If the interrupt is not pending or present on the CPU interface, the Clear command has no effect. However, the CPU interface must still issue a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) response.

**Note**

A Clear command with INTID = 1023 has no effect, but a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) response must still be generated.

#### <span id="page-897-1"></span>**A.4.4 Clear Acknowledge (ICC)**

The CPU interface sends a Clear Acknowledge response to acknowledge the receipt of a [Clear](#page-897-0) or [VClear](#page-909-2) command. [Figure](#page-897-3) A-5 shows the Clear Acknowledge response format.

![](_page_897_Figure_16.jpeg)

**Figure A-5 Clear Acknowledge**

<span id="page-897-3"></span>In [Figure](#page-897-3) A-5, V indicates the original command to which the Clear Acknowledge corresponds:

**0** The Clear Acknowledge corresponds to a [Clear](#page-897-0) command.

**1** The Clear Acknowledge corresponds to a [VClear](#page-909-2) command.

**Note**

No INTID field is required for this command because only a single [Clear](#page-897-0) can be outstanding for a CPU interface at any time.

#### <span id="page-898-1"></span><span id="page-898-0"></span>**A.4.5 Deactivate (ICC)**

The Deactivate command deactivates an interrupt, provided the initiating Exception level and Security state can access the interrupt group to which the INTID belongs. The Redistributor sends a [Deactivate Acknowledge](#page-900-1) in response to a Deactivate command. [Figure](#page-898-2) A-6 shows the Deactivate command format.

![](_page_898_Figure_3.jpeg)

**Figure A-6 Deactivate**

#### <span id="page-898-2"></span>In [Figure](#page-898-2) A-6:

| • | Groups indicates the interrupt groups that the initiating Exception level and Security state are permitted to |
|---|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|   | modify:                                                                                                       |

**Bit[10]** When this bit is set to 1, Secure Group 1 interrupts can be modified.

**Bit[9]** When this bit is set to 1, Non-secure Group 1 interrupts can be modified.

**Bit[8]** When this bit is set to 1, Group 0 interrupts can be modified.

**Note**

When sending a Deactivate command, at least one of the Groups bits must be set to 1. A protocol error occurs if none of these bits are set to 1.

- ID length indicates the number of INTID bits the Deactivate command includes. See *[Supported INTID sizes](#page-888-1) [on page](#page-888-1) A-889* for more information. The Deactivate command applies only to physical SPIs, PPIs, and SGIs, each of which has INTIDs no higher than 8192. This field must therefore be set to 0b00, indicating a 16-bit INTID. The CPU interface does not generate Deactivate packets for LPIs.
- INTID is the 32-bit value read from the corresponding interrupt acknowledge cycle that is presented in the write to [ICC\\_EOIR0\\_EL1](#page-244-0) or [ICC\\_EOIR1\\_EL1](#page-246-0).

**Note**

There is no requirement for the CPU interface to have received the corresponding [Activate Acknowledge](#page-895-1) command before sending the Deactivate command.

When System register access is enabled for the initiating Exception level and Security state, one of the Groups bits is set according to the rules in *[Groups field when System register access is enabled on page](#page-899-0) A-900*.

**Note**

In an implementation that supports two Security states, for Secure EL1 to be permitted to handle Group 1 interrupts, that is, IRQs not taken to EL3, both bit[9] and bit[10] must be set to 1.

When System register access is not enabled for the initiating Exception level and Security state, the Groups field is set according to the Security state of the initiating Exception level. That is, bit [9] is set to 1 for Non-secure write access, and bits [10:8] are all set to 1 for Secure write access. In an implementation that supports only a single Security state, write accesses that result in the generation of a [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command are treated as Secure writes.

In an implementation that supports two Security states, Group 0 and Secure Group 1 interrupts can be modified only from a Secure initiating Exception level. This includes EL3, regardless of the setting of [SCR\\_EL3](#page-29-4).NS. In an implementation that supports only a single Security state, the Redistributor can ignore bit[10].

![](_page_899_Picture_1.jpeg)

The Redistributor must send a [Deactivate Acknowledge](#page-900-1) in response to a [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command.

- If affinity routing is enabled for an interrupt group, the Redistributor must acknowledge, but otherwise ignore, any [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command with a reserved INTID.
- If affinity routing is not enabled for an interrupt group, the Redistributor must acknowledge, but otherwise ignore any [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command with an ID in the range 1019 < INTID < 8192 where bits [9:4] are not 0. That is, it might issue [Deactivate](#page-898-1) packets for SGIs with a non-zero CPU number in bits[12:10] of [GICC\\_IAR](#page-756-1).
- If affinity routing is not enabled for an interrupt group and the ID specifies an SGI, and the PE specified by the CPU number in bits[12:10] does not support operation when affinity routing is not enabled, the Redistributor must acknowledge but otherwise ignore the [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command.

#### <span id="page-899-0"></span>**Groups field when System register access is enabled**

When System register access is enabled for the initiating Exception level and Security state, the following pseudocode describes the rules for specifying the value of the Groups field:

```
// DeactivateGroups_SRE()
// ======================
(boolean,boolean,boolean) DeactivateGroups_SRE(bits(2) effective_EL)
    boolean groups_G0S = FALSE;
    boolean groups_G1NS = FALSE;
    boolean groups_G1S = FALSE;
    if effective_EL == EL3 then
        groups_G0S = TRUE;
        groups_G1NS = TRUE;
        groups_G1S = GICD_CTLR.DS == '0';
    elsif effective_EL == EL2 && IsSecure() then
       // Secure EL2
       // This also covers the case when the HW bit is one in a List Register
       // corresponding to a write at Secure EL1
       groups_G0S = !HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.FIQ == '0';
       groups_G1NS = !HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.IRQ == '0';
       groups_G1S = (!HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.IRQ == '0') && GICD_CTLR.DS == '0';
    elsif effective_EL == EL2 && !IsSecure() then
       // Non-secure EL2
       // This also covers the case when the HW bit is one in a List Register
       // corresponding to a write at Non-secure EL1
       groups_G0S = (!HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.FIQ == '0') && GICD_CTLR.DS == '1';
       groups_G1NS = !HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.IRQ == '0';
    elsif effective_EL == EL1 && IsSecure() then
        // Secure EL1
        groups_G0S = (!HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.FIQ == '0') && (SCR_EL3.EEL2 == '0' || HCR_EL2.FMO == '0');
        groups_G1NS = (!HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.IRQ == '0') && (SCR_EL3.EEL2 == '0' || HCR_EL2.IMO ==
'0');
       groups_G1S = (!HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.IRQ == '0') && (SCR_EL3.EEL2 == '0' || HCR_EL2.IMO == '0')
&& GICD_CTLR.DS == '0';
    elsif effective_EL == EL1 && !IsSecure() then
        // Non-secure EL1
        groups_G0S = (!HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.FIQ == '0') && (!HaveEL(EL2) || HCR_EL2.FMO == '0') &&
GICD_CTLR.DS == '1';
        groups_G1NS = (!HaveEL(EL3) || SCR_EL3.IRQ == '0') && (!HaveEL(EL2) || HCR_EL2.IMO == '0');
    return (groups_G1S, groups_G1NS, groups_G0S);
```

![](_page_900_Figure_1.jpeg)

When FEAT\_RME is implemented, accesses from Realm state are treated identically to those from Non-secure state.

If the Deactivate command relates to a virtual interrupt that has a corresponding physical interrupt in the List registers, that is [ICH\\_LR<n>\\_EL2](#page-352-0).HW is set to 1, a virtual write caused the deactivation of the physical interrupt.

The bits are set as if an equivalent write had been performed at EL2. That is, effective\_EL == 2.

#### <span id="page-900-1"></span>**A.4.6 Deactivate Acknowledge (IRI)**

The Redistributor sends a Deactivate Acknowledge response to confirm receipt of a [Deactivate](#page-898-1) command, and to confirm that the effects of the deactivate operation are visible to the Redistributor and other PEs. [Figure](#page-900-2) A-7 shows the Deactivate Acknowledge response format.

![](_page_900_Figure_7.jpeg)

**Figure A-7 Deactivate Acknowledge**

#### <span id="page-900-2"></span><span id="page-900-0"></span>**A.4.7 Downstream Control (IRI)**

The Downstream Control command transfers a specified number of bytes of data to the CPU interface. [Figure](#page-900-3) A-8 shows the Downstream Control command format.

![](_page_900_Figure_11.jpeg)

**Figure A-8 Downstream Control**

#### <span id="page-900-3"></span>In [Figure](#page-900-3) A-8:

• Length indicates the number of bytes of valid data appended to the 2 byte header.

If this field specifies a number of bytes that is not exactly divisible by the interface width, as *[Signals and the](#page-886-1)  [GIC Stream Protocol on page](#page-886-1) A-887* describes, any surplus bytes beyond this specified length in the last transfer must be zero. The CPU interface must ignore such bytes.

<span id="page-901-1"></span>• Identifier is a value that specifies the format of the data provided, and can have the values shown in [Table](#page-901-1) A-7 [on page](#page-901-1) A-902.

**Table A-7 Downstream Control Identifier values**

| Data value name                   | Identifier<br>value | Length | Contents                                                                                        |  |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--|
| Settings (configure<br>interface) | 0x00<br>0x1         |        | Data[0] holds the Redistributor global settings, and these bits have the<br>following meanings: |  |
|                                   |                     |        | [7:6]<br>VL. Indicates the supported vINTID length.                                             |  |
|                                   |                     |        | [5:4]<br>PL. Indicates the supported pINTID length.                                             |  |
|                                   |                     |        | [3:2]<br>Reserved. RES0.                                                                        |  |
|                                   |                     |        | RSS. Indicates the value of GICD_TYPER.RSS.<br>[1]                                              |  |
|                                   |                     |        | [0]<br>DS. Disable Security. Indicates the value of GICD_CTLR.DS.                               |  |
|                                   |                     |        | Note<br>Bit[0] is set to 1 if the GIC supports only a single Security state.                    |  |
| Reserved                          | 0x01 - 0x7F         | -      | -                                                                                               |  |
| IMPLEMENTATION<br>DEFINED         | 0x80 - 0xFF         | -      | Reserved for IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED variables.                                                  |  |

**Note** Each identifier value can have a different length, but a particular identifier value must always have the same length.

The CPU interface must always respond to a Downstream Control command with a [Downstream Control](#page-901-0)  [Acknowledge](#page-901-0) response.

After the CPU interface receives a Downstream Control command where DS == 1, a packet protocol violation occurs if it receives a subsequent Downstream Control command where DS == 0, before an intervening hardware reset.

If a CPU interface receives an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED value that it cannot interpret, this constitutes a protocol error. See *[Software generation of protocol errors and packet errors on page](#page-888-0) A-889*.

**Note**

The IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED values of the Downstream Write Command must only be used where the Distributor and the CPU interface interpret the IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED values to mean the same thing. This is typically the case where both components have been produced as part of the same system design.

#### <span id="page-901-0"></span>**A.4.8 Downstream Control Acknowledge (ICC)**

The CPU interface sends a Downstream Control Acknowledge response to confirm receipt of a [Downstream](#page-900-0)  [Control](#page-900-0) command. [Figure](#page-901-2) A-9 shows the Downstream Control Acknowledge response format.

![](_page_901_Figure_13.jpeg)

**Figure A-9 Downstream Control Acknowledge**

<span id="page-901-2"></span>In [Figure](#page-901-2) A-9:

• VL indicates the virtual INTID length, that is, the supported number of INTID bits.

PL indicates the physical INTID length, that is, the supported number of INTID bits.

See Supported INTID sizes on page A-889 for more information.

VL must be set to the minimum of:

- The value of VL contained in the first Downstream Control command received after reset.
- The value that ICH\_VTR\_EL2.IDbits specifies.

PL must be set to the minimum of:

- The value of PL contained in the first Downstream Control command received after reset.
- The value that ICC\_CTLR\_EL3.IDbits or ICC\_CTLR\_EL1.IDbits, as appropriate, specifies.

#### <span id="page-902-1"></span><span id="page-902-0"></span>A.4.9 Generate SGI (ICC)

The CPU interface sends a Generate SGI command to the Redistributor to generate an SGI. The Redistributor sends a Generate SGI Acknowledge in response to a Generate SGI command. Figure A-10 shows the Generate SGI command format.

| 15 1                      | 2 11           | 10 | 9   | 8   | 1   | б  | 5  | 4  | 3 |           | U |
|---------------------------|----------------|----|-----|-----|-----|----|----|----|---|-----------|---|
| SGInum                    | 0              | 0  | RSV | A3V | IRM | NS | SC | ЭT |   | 0x7       |   |
| Target List               |                |    |     |     |     |    |    |    |   |           |   |
| A2                        |                |    |     | A1  |     |    |    |    |   |           |   |
| Reserved 0x0 <sup>a</sup> | Range Selector |    |     |     |     |    | A: | 3ª |   | <br> <br> |   |

a. Whether this part of the packet is transmitted depends on the value of A3V and RSV.

Figure A-10 Generate SGI

#### <span id="page-902-2"></span>In Figure A-10:

- SGInum indicates the INTID of the SGI to be generated.
- RSV (Range Selector Valid) indicates whether the RS field is valid:
  - **0** RS is RESO.
  - 1 RS indicates the affinities covered by Target List.
- A3V indicates whether the command includes an A3 field. When A3V is 0, the packet does not include an A3 field, and the Redistributor must use 0 as the value of A3. When a CPU interface supports the Aff3 field and a write to ICC\_SGI0R, ICC\_SGI1R or ICC\_ASGI1R specifies Aff3 == 0, the resulting packet must clear A3V to zero.
- IRM indicates the Interrupt Routing Mode to be used. When IRM is set to 1, Target List, A1, A2, and A3 are ignored. The A3V field is RES0.

| Note |  |  |  |
|------|--|--|--|

Software might specify one or more target affinities that are not implemented by the system. Arm expects the Generate SGI packets generated by the CPU interface to report all the affinities specified by software.

- NS indicates whether the Generate SGI command originates from Non-secure state:
  - **0** The command originates from a Secure Execution state.
  - 1 The command originates from a Non-secure Execution state.

• SGT specifies the register access that caused the Generate SGI command:

0b00 [ICC\\_SGI0R\\_EL1](#page-272-0). 0b01 [ICC\\_SGI1R\\_EL1](#page-275-0). 0b10 [ICC\\_ASGI1R\\_EL1.](#page-222-0) 0b11 Reserved.

When the Redistributor supports two Security states and affinity routing is not enabled for the Secure state in the Redistributor, Generate SGI commands that correspond to Non-secure writes to [ICC\\_SGI0R\\_EL1](#page-272-0) and [ICC\\_ASGI1R\\_EL1](#page-222-0) must be acknowledged and discarded, and must not set an SGI pending.

When the Redistributor supports a single Security state, that is, [GICD\\_CTLR](#page-543-0).DS == 1, Generate SGI commands that correspond to Non-secure writes to [ICC\\_SGI0R\\_EL1](#page-272-0) or [ICC\\_ASGI1R\\_EL1](#page-222-0) generate a Group 0 SGI.

- Target List is the group of target PEs defined by the routing mode. For SGIs, the GIC routing mode defines a group of target PEs, targetlist. This field is treated as defined in [ICC\\_SGI0R\\_EL1](#page-272-0), [ICC\\_SGI1R\\_EL1,](#page-275-0) and [ICC\\_ASGI1R\\_EL1](#page-222-0).
- A1, A2, and A3 are the affinity level values used for generating the set of target PEs. These fields are treated in the same way as the Affinity value fields in [ICC\\_SGI0R\\_EL1,](#page-272-0) [ICC\\_SGI1R\\_EL1,](#page-275-0) and [ICC\\_ASGI1R\\_EL1](#page-222-0) Whether the A3 field is supported is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED.

**Note**

In systems where the Redistributor only supports the zero value for A3, the Redistributor must acknowledge any Generate SGI commands where A3V == 1 with a [Generate SGI Acknowledge](#page-903-2) response, but must otherwise ignore the command.

• RS (Range Selector) indicates the affinities covered by Target List. This field is treated as defined in [ICC\\_SGI0R\\_EL1,](#page-272-0) [ICC\\_SGI1R\\_EL1,](#page-275-0) and [ICC\\_ASGI1R\\_EL1](#page-222-0).

#### <span id="page-903-2"></span>**A.4.10 Generate SGI Acknowledge (IRI)**

The Redistributor sends a Generate SGI Acknowledge response to confirm that it has received a [Generate SGI](#page-902-1) command from the CPU interface, and that the effects of that command are guaranteed to become visible to other PEs. [Figure](#page-903-3) A-11 shows the Generate SGI Acknowledge response format.

![](_page_903_Figure_13.jpeg)

**Figure A-11 Generate SGI Acknowledge**

**Note**

Receipt of a Generate SGI Acknowledge response by a CPU interface does not guarantee that the corresponding SGI pending state is set, but it does guarantee that the pending state will become set.

#### <span id="page-903-4"></span><span id="page-903-3"></span><span id="page-903-1"></span><span id="page-903-0"></span>**A.4.11 Quiesce (IRI)**

The Redistributor sends a Quiesce command to request that the CPU interface enters the quiescent state. [Figure](#page-903-4) A-12 shows the Quiesce command format.

![](_page_903_Figure_19.jpeg)

**Figure A-12 Quiesce**

A CPU interface is quiescent when there are no pending interrupts and all outstanding operations are complete. To ensure quiescence, a CPU interface must:

- Respond to any outstanding [Clear](#page-897-0) and [VClear](#page-909-2) commands by sending a [Clear Acknowledge](#page-897-1) command.
- [Release](#page-904-1) any pending virtual or physical interrupts.
- Ensure it receives an acknowledge response from the Redistributor to indicate completion of all outstanding:
  - [Generate SGI](#page-902-1) requests.
  - [Activate](#page-895-0) requests.
  - [Deactivate](#page-898-1) requests.
  - [Upstream Control](#page-906-0).
- Respond to the Quiesce commands by sending a [Quiesce Acknowledge](#page-904-2) response as the final transfer.

In addition, software must ensure that the Redistributor receives no traffic after the CPU interface sends the [Quiesce](#page-904-2)  [Acknowledge](#page-904-2) response. Failure to adhere to this result in UNPREDICTABLE behavior. In practice, because such timing is not predictable, software must ensure that no traffic is generated after the [GICR\\_WAKER](#page-727-0).ProcessorSleep bit is set to 1, see Chapter 11 *[Power Management](#page-186-1)* .

A CPU interface cannot receive a Quiesce command if a [Downstream Control Acknowledge](#page-901-0) response is outstanding. See *[Rules associated with the downstream Redistributor commands on page](#page-891-1) A-892* for more information.

#### <span id="page-904-2"></span>**A.4.12 Quiesce Acknowledge (ICC)**

The CPU interface sends a Quiesce Acknowledge response to confirm receipt of a [Quiesce](#page-903-1) command, and to confirm that it is quiescent. [Figure](#page-904-3) A-13 shows the Quiesce Acknowledge response format.

![](_page_904_Figure_14.jpeg)

**Figure A-13 Quiesce Acknowledge**

The [Quiesce](#page-903-1) command acts as a form of barrier. Before sending a Quiesce Acknowledge response, the CPU interface must be quiescent, that is, it must fulfill the requirements for quiescence specified in *[Quiesce \(IRI\) on](#page-903-1)  page [A-904](#page-903-1)*.

#### <span id="page-904-3"></span><span id="page-904-1"></span><span id="page-904-0"></span>**A.4.13 Release (ICC)**

The CPU interface logic sends a Release response when it cannot handle a particular interrupt. [Figure](#page-904-4) A-14 shows the Release response format.

![](_page_904_Figure_19.jpeg)

a. If the command includes this field, bits[31:24] are 0.

**Figure A-14 Release**

#### <span id="page-904-4"></span>In [Figure](#page-904-4) A-14:

• ID length indicates the number of INTID bits the Release response includes. See *[Supported INTID sizes on](#page-888-1)  page [A-889](#page-888-1)* for more information.

- V indicates the original command to which the Release response corresponds:
  - **0** The Release corresponds to a [Set](#page-905-0) command.
  - **1** The Release corresponds to a [VSet](#page-909-1) command.
- INTID is the value that the CPU interface returns after a valid read of [ICC\\_IAR0\\_EL1](#page-252-0) or [ICC\\_IAR1\\_EL1.](#page-254-0)

![](_page_905_Figure_6.jpeg)

- During legacy operation, the INTID that is returned for SGIs includes the source PE in the [GICC\\_IAR.](#page-756-1)Source\_CPU\_ID field.
- If the INTID corresponds to an interrupt that uses the 1 of N model, the Redistributor might forward the interrupt to a different PE or it might send the interrupt to the same PE again. See *[Priority-based](#page-893-0)  [routing on page](#page-893-0) A-894* for information about how the PMHE field might affect the 1 of N selection.

If the CPU interface issues a Release response as a result of disabling an interrupt group, Arm recommends that it sends the [Upstream Control](#page-906-0) command that contains the revised interrupt group enable information before issuing the Release response.

#### <span id="page-905-0"></span>**A.4.14 Set (IRI)**

The Set command sets the highest priority pending interrupt for a PE. The PE has control of the interrupt and might respond to a read of [ICC\\_IAR0\\_EL1](#page-252-0) or [ICC\\_IAR1\\_EL1](#page-254-0) with the INTID. [Figure](#page-905-1) A-15 shows the Set command format.

![](_page_905_Figure_12.jpeg)

**Figure A-15 Set**

#### <span id="page-905-1"></span>In [Figure](#page-905-1) A-15:

- Priority indicates the actual priority of the interrupt, that is, the Secure, unshifted view. Bits corresponding to unimplemented priority bits in the CPU interface are RES0.
- ID length indicates the number of INTID bits the Set command includes. See *[Supported INTID sizes on](#page-888-1)  page [A-889](#page-888-1)* for more information.
- Mod represents the value of the [GICD\\_IGRPMODR<n>.](#page-569-0)Group status bit for the interrupt.
- Grp represents the interrupt group, as indicated by the corresponding [GICD\\_IGROUPR<n>](#page-565-0).Group status bit.
- INTID is the value that the CPU interface returns after a valid read of an [ICC\\_IAR0\\_EL1](#page-252-0) or [ICC\\_IAR1\\_EL1](#page-254-0).

**Note**

During legacy operation, the INTID that is returned for SGIs includes the source PE in the [GICC\\_IAR.](#page-756-1)Source\_CPU\_ID field.

A GICv3.3 Redistributor does not forward interrupts with a priority of 0xFF to a CPU interface.

In GICv3.3, when SET.{Mod, Grp} indicates any of the following, a SET.priority of 0xFF indicates that the interrupt has the non-maskable property:

- Group 1.
- Secure Group 1.
- Non-Secure Group 1.

The priority of the non-maskable interrupt is treated as one of the following:

• For Non-secure Group 1, the priority is 0x80.

- For Secure Group 1, the priority is 0x00.
- For Group 1, the priority is 0x00.

| Note |  |
|------|--|
|      |  |

The behavior described above does not depend on the SCTLR\_ELx.NMI value of the current Exception level or of the target Exception level.

A SET packet for a Group 0 interrupt with priority == 0xFF is unchanged from GICv3.0, and indicatesthe interrupt's priority is 0xFF. A GICv3.3 Redistributor does not generate this combination.

If the Redistributor sends a Set command, the interrupt specified in the command replaces any outstanding highest pending interrupt, that is, the command sets a new highest priority pending interrupt. Where a pending interrupt is replaced, the CPU interface must [Release](#page-904-1) it back to the Redistributor.

The Redistributor must:

- Ensure that no more than two Set commands that are waiting for a response are outstanding per PE at any time.
- Send a Set command only if it can accept an [Activate](#page-895-0) command where V == 0.

![](_page_906_Picture_10.jpeg)

An implementation can guarantee this by treating the Set command as outstanding until either a [Release](#page-904-1) command is received for the Set command, or an [Activate Acknowledge](#page-895-1) response is sent for the corresponding [Activate](#page-895-0).

- Never send a Set command when any of the following conditions apply:
  - The INTID is a special interrupt number, that is, 1020-1023.
  - Affinity routing is enabled for an interrupt group and the INTID value is invalid.
  - Affinity routing is not enabled for an interrupt group, 1023 < INTID < 8192, and bits[9:4] are non-zero. That is, the Redistributor is permitted to send Set commands for SGIs where bits[12:10] of [ICC\\_IAR0\\_EL1](#page-252-0) or [ICC\\_IAR1\\_EL1](#page-254-0) specify the CPUID of the source PE.
  - Affinity routing is not enabled for an interrupt group, and INTID > 8191
  - The Set command has the same INTID as a previous Set command, unless the Redistributor has received an [Activate](#page-895-0) command or [Release](#page-904-1) response.

The Redistributor must not send a SET command for an interrupt until all of the following are true:

- All previous outstanding SET commands for that interrupt have been returned through a [Release](#page-904-1) or [Activate](#page-895-0) command.
- The interrupt is in the pending state, see *[Interrupt handling state machine on page](#page-55-0) 4-56*.

If the interrupt group is disabled, the CPU interface cannot handle the interrupt, and must [Release](#page-904-1) the interrupt.

#### <span id="page-906-1"></span><span id="page-906-0"></span>**A.4.15 Upstream Control (ICC)**

• Identifier is a value that specifies the format of the data provided.

The Redistributor sends an Upstream Control Acknowledge response to confirm receipt of an [Upstream Control](#page-906-0) command, and to confirm that the effects of the write operation are visible to the Distributor. [Figure](#page-908-1) A-17 shows the Upstream Control Acknowledge response format.

![](_page_908_Figure_6.jpeg)

**Figure A-17 Upstream Control Acknowledge**

#### <span id="page-909-2"></span>**A.4.17 VClear (IRI)**

The VClear command resets the highest priority pending virtual interrupt.

This command is provided in GICv4 only.

[Figure](#page-909-3) A-18 shows the VClear command format.

![](_page_909_Figure_5.jpeg)

a. If the command includes this field, bits[31:24] are 0.

#### <span id="page-909-3"></span>In [Figure](#page-909-3) A-18:
